name: AI Deep Dive — KRC — 2026-05-02
rationale: Kilroy Realty Corp is a West Coast tech campus office REIT facing secular headwinds from remote work adoption. GAAP DCF gives $15.74 SELL (-53.2%), but this materially understates cash generation — the EBITDA margin is 70.5% and Piotroski is 7/9, with leverage decreasing and ROA improving. A proper FFO analysis at 12x P/FFO would suggest $30-40/share (close to current). The GAAP SELL signal is a methodology artifact for REITs — investors must interpret with this caveat. Analyst consensus: Hold at $35.50 target, essentially fairly valued.

Revenue declines 3% CAGR as leases expire and renewal rates are lower. GAAP margin 6% reflects analyst-implied earnings trajectory (Y1 $0.56 EPS / $1.07B = 5.6%). Tech layoffs in San Francisco/LA/Seattle reduce office absorption. Interest rate headwinds on refinancing at higher rates. Exit PE 15x on compressed GAAP earnings = $3.71 PV.

Note: FFO-adjusted base would give ~$30-35 (see analyticsLog for REIT methodology caveat). Y5 PV $15.07 per GAAP DCF.

KRC's properties in San Francisco, LA, and Seattle become the most sought-after locations for AI labs requiring proximity to engineering talent. Revenue grows 4% CAGR with strong lease renewal pricing. GAAP margin 12% recovers toward historical 18-25% range as gains on AI-driven property value appreciation supplement rental income. Exit PE 40x: data center REIT premium applied to AI-adjacent office REIT. Y5 PV $38.31 — the only scenario where stock is approximately fairly valued at current prices.

aiThesis.rationale: Kilroy Realty Corp is a high-quality office REIT facing secular headwinds that make traditional GAAP DCF an unreliable valuation tool. The GAAP DCF gives $15.74 SELL (-53%), but this is primarily a methodology artifact: the EBITDA margin is 70.5% and the Piotroski score is 7/9 — indicating a fundamentally healthy business. The GAAP net margin is distorted by depreciation on $10B+ of office real estate assets (~$300M/yr D&A). Analysts expect GAAP EPS to collapse from $2.33 TTM to $0.56 in Y1 — not because the business is deteriorating, but because normalized D&A expense is running through the P&L without the offsetting property sale gains that inflated prior GAAP earnings. A proper FFO analysis (adding back ~$2/share in D&A) would give FFO/share of ~$2.50-3.50, implying a current P/FFO of 10-13x — at the low end of the historical office REIT range of 10-18x. This suggests the stock is approximately fairly valued at current prices on a cash-flow basis, consistent with the analyst HOLD consensus ($35.50 target). The primary risk is structural: WFH is real, West Coast tech offices are most affected, and any further reduction in leased square footage would impair revenue. The primary opportunity is AI-driven office demand — AI/ML teams require significant collaboration space, and KRC's premium tech campus properties are well-positioned. SELL on GAAP DCF. Investors in this name should use FFO-based analysis, not EPS-based DCF.

analyticsLog.marginAnchor: REIT accounting distortion. GAAP net margin history: 21.2% → 18.8% → 18.6% → 24.8% (TTM). Appears mean-reverting around 21%. HOWEVER: analyst Y1 EPS $0.56 / $1.07B revenue = 5.6% forward GAAP margin — a dramatic collapse from 24.8% TTM. This likely reflects: (1) normalized depreciation on real estate assets ($300M+/yr D&A); (2) reduced gains on property sales; (3) lease expiration losses. The EBITDA margin of 70.5% is the true operating metric for this office REIT — the GAAP margin suppression is artificial. Using 8% base GAAP margin (above analyst Y1 6%, reflecting 5-year recovery trend). This is a declining-trend situation for GAAP metrics, not mean-reverting.
analyticsLog.growthDerivation: Analyst Y1 $1.069B (-3.6%), Y2 $1.103B (+3.2%). Revenue essentially flat — office REIT in stabilization phase. Base 2% CAGR is slightly above analyst blended flat consensus, reflecting modest AI demand recovery by Y3-Y5. Bear -3% = continued WFH pressure. Bull +4% = AI office boom.
analyticsLog.sectorBenchmarkRow: Real Estate — REIT Office: GAAP P/E typically 15-40x (suppressed by D&A). FFO P/E typically 10-18x for office REITs. Current TTM P/E 18.4x on $2.33 EPS, but forward PE 67.3x on $0.50 EPS (real estate depreciation collapses GAAP earnings). Benchmark office REIT exit multiples: bear 15x, base 28x (AI premium), bull 40x. EBITDA multiple 70.5% is extraordinary for any asset class.
dataQualityFlags: REIT ACCOUNTING DISTORTION: GAAP net margin (18-25% historical) will compress to ~6% forward per analyst EPS estimates. This is driven by D&A on $10B+ office portfolio, not operational deterioration. EBITDA margin 70.5% is the correct cash generation metric. DCF SELL verdict ($15.74) is a GAAP methodology artifact — FFO-adjusted analysis would give ~$30-40/share.

Analyst EPS Y1 $0.56 vs TTM $2.33 — 76% EPS collapse on flat revenue. This is not a business deterioration — it is a normalization of GAAP earnings after above-normal property sale gains in prior periods.

West Coast tech campus concentration: KRC's portfolio is almost entirely San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, and Seattle. Significant geographic concentration risk in markets most affected by tech layoffs and WFH adoption.
Forward PE 67.3x appears extreme but is a REIT artifact — FFO/share is likely $2.50-3.50 vs GAAP EPS $0.50-0.56.
